---
title: "BVSGH: FLC data"
output: html_document
---

This example runs the proposed method on the serum free light chain data (main text Section 7.1).
The chains here are shorter than in the paper, so the probabilities differ slightly.

```{r setup, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE}
#knitr::opts_chunk$set(comment = "")
library(mvtnorm); library(survival); library(glmnet)
BVS_CORE <- normalizePath("./core")
source(file.path(BVS_CORE, "ADS_sampler.R"))
source(file.path(BVS_CORE, "utils", "map_estimates.R"))
source("real_application/prepare_data.R")

# labeling of model string
role <- c("1" = "^time", "2" = "^haz", "3" = "", "4" = "")
label <- function(s, vars) {
  g <- strsplit(s, "")[[1]]; i <- which(g != "0")
  if (!length(i)) return("null")
  paste0("{", paste0(vars[i], role[g[i]], collapse = ", "), "}^", gam2haz(s))
}
```

## Data

Each covariate enters the model through $\gamma_j$: 0 (excluded), 1 (time level, AH), 2 (hazard
level, PH), 3 (both levels, GH) or 4 (AFT). `prep.flchain()` returns the response `y`, the event
indicator `status` and the design matrices `x` (hazard level) and `xt` (time level).

```{r data}
dat <- prep.flchain("orig", file = "real_application/data/flchain.csv")  # "trans": Kappa and Lambda replaced by their sum and ratio
vars <- colnames(dat$x)
c(n = nrow(dat$x), p = ncol(dat$x), censored = round(1 - mean(dat$status), 3))
```

## Running the sampler

The initial model comes from a Cox-LASSO fit followed by stepwise selection (`init.gam`).
`BVS.MCMC` is run once for the selected prior on the model-specific coefficients, 
with the default model-space prior.

```{r run}
set.seed(1234)
modelpar <- list(inits = list(nu = rnorm(1), theta0 = rnorm(1),
                              theta = rnorm(ncol(dat$xt), 0, 0.5), 
                              eta = rnorm(ncol(dat$x), 0, 0.5),
                              g.theta = 1, g.eta = 1, 
                              g = 1, 
                              a_g = NULL,
                              gam = init.gam(dat, history.keep = FALSE),
                              nu.alpha = 0.01, nu.beta = 0.01),
                 data = dat)
mcmcpar <- list(n.iter = 10000, n.burnin = 2000, n.thin = 10, n.chain = 1, printevery = 1e9)
fits <- BVS.MCMC(modelpar, mcmcpar, gprior.mat = "LCM", # or "Product", "LCM-hyper"
                 gamprior = "default", verbose = FALSE)
```

## Results

`post.prob` lists every model evaluated by the sampler, with its posterior probability
renormalised over these models.

```{r top}
pp <- head(fits$post.prob, 5)
data.frame(model = sapply(pp$Vars, label, vars = vars), prob = round(pp$prob, 3), row.names = NULL)
```

Posterior probabilities of the hazard structures:

```{r hazard}
round(fits$haz.post, 3)
```

Posterior inclusion probabilities, overall and at the time and hazard levels:

```{r pip}
pp <- fits$post.prob
G <- do.call(rbind, lapply(strsplit(pp$Vars, ""), as.integer))
pip <- rbind(any = colSums(pp$prob * (G != 0)), as.matrix(fits$PIP.post))
dimnames(pip) <- list(c("included", "time level", "hazard level"), vars)
round(pip, 3)
```

MAP estimates of the time-level ($\alpha$) and hazard-level ($\beta$) coefficients of the top
model:

```{r map}
gam.top <- as.integer(strsplit(pp$Vars[1], "")[[1]])
M <- map.lcm(gam.top, dat)
used <- gam.top != 0
data.frame(variable = vars[used], alpha = round(M$alpha[used], 3), beta = round(M$beta[used], 3))
```
